summary: Backend-only testing for Snagging Lists V2. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_snagging_v2.py (38 tests) covering reference, create/validate, filters (project/status/priority/assignedTo/overdue/assignedToMe/q), PATCH/DELETE (soft), full lifecycle (assign/status/comment/photos/verify/close/reopen with audit history + closedAt/completionDate semantics), stats, per-project summary, templates roundtrip, global search by snagRef, /api/attention (snag_overdue + snag_critical kinds present), cross-user isolation vs sparky01, and regression on contracts/purchase-orders/invoice-builder/applications-for-payment/variation-orders /reference and /stats endpoints. All 38 tests PASS (100%).

minor.issue: Deleting a non-existent photo id returns 200 (idempotent). Not a defect per spec but worth confirming whether a 404 was intended for parity with comment deletion (comment delete also returns 200 idempotently).
Same idempotent 200 behaviour for unknown comment id.

action_items: Optional: decide whether DELETE of unknown photo/comment id should return 404 for consistency with other resource-level 404s (currently 200).
critical_code_review_comments: snagging.py is ~610 lines — approaching the 700-line split threshold; consider splitting lifecycle endpoints, templates, and attention/collectors into separate modules soon.

get_user(token) is called with `authorization.replace('Bearer ', '')` at the top of every endpoint (25+ times). Extract a shared dependency (fastapi.Depends) to remove duplication and centralise auth error handling.
list_snags applies `q`, `overdue`, `assignedToMe` filters in Python after loading up to 2000 rows — fine for now, but should push to Mongo query as volume grows.

assignedToMe logic has Python operator-precedence ambiguity: `(a).lower()==me or (b).lower()==my_email and my_email!=''` — works but relies on `and` binding tighter than `or`; add explicit parentheses for readability.

Auto-move Open→Assigned on create only checks `doc.get('status')=='Open'`; if caller explicitly sends another status alongside assignedTo, no history entry is created. Acceptable, but document behaviour.

closedAt is stored as a full ISO string, but `closed_at.startswith(today)` for closedToday is UTC-only; users in other timezones may see off-by-one. Consider storing/comparing with a project timezone.
seed_data_creation: All test data prefixed 'TEST ' and soft-deleted in test_zzz_cleanup.
